source: វិទ្យាការទប់ស្កាត់ និងកម្ចាត់សមាសភាពបទព្រុងលើដំណាំទុរេន (Prevention and Control of Harmful Organisms on Durian), Cambodian technical extension document compiled with reference to CABI Crop Protection Compendium and durian pest/disease literature, 28pp
text: Stem and patch canker, caused by the fungus/oomycete Phytophthora palmivora, is described in this source as one of the most serious and economically damaging durian diseases. It appears as a dark, wet-looking, sunken lesion (canker) on the trunk or main branches, often oozing a reddish-brown gum, and can girdle and kill the branch or, if it reaches the trunk base, the whole tree. The same pathogen also causes root rot and fruit rot in durian (see the separate root-rot entry), so an orchard with canker symptoms on trunks should also be checked for root symptoms and vice versa. Conditions that favor the disease include poor drainage, waterlogged soil, wounds on the bark (from pruning, mechanical damage, or borer entry holes) and prolonged high humidity around the trunk base from weeds or mulch piled directly against the bark. General control approach: improve drainage, keep the trunk base clear of weeds and mulch, avoid wounding the bark unnecessarily, scrape out and treat cankers with fungicide paste as soon as they are spotted, and remove and destroy severely affected trees to prevent the pathogen from building up in the orchard soil.
